inspiration.name: Linux Kernel Map
inspiration.usage: Layered organizing model only; no text, node descriptions, or diagram content copied.

layers.name: User-space interfaces
layers.purpose: System calls, ioctls, and other entry points from userspace into the kernel.

layers.name: Virtual subsystems
layers.purpose: Filesystem, networking, and block abstractions that hide hardware differences.

layers.name: Bridges
layers.purpose: Glue between virtual subsystems and the hardware-facing layers.

layers.name: Logical subsystems
layers.purpose: Core kernel services: scheduling, memory management, IPC, time, security.

layers.name: Hardware interfaces
layers.purpose: Device model, driver core, buses, and architecture-specific code.

layers.name: Hardware
layers.purpose: The physical devices and buses the kernel drives.

areas.title: Syscall entry
areas.summary: The path from a userspace syscall instruction to the kernel function that implements it.

symbols.name: do_sys_openat2
symbols.purpose: Common implementation behind openat and openat2.

symbols.name: ksys_read
symbols.purpose: Kernel-side implementation of read(2).

symbols.name: vfs_read
symbols.purpose: Calls the file's read operation after permission checks.

areas.title: Process and scheduling
areas.summary: Task selection, context switching, and the schedule() entry point.

symbols.name: schedule
symbols.purpose: Entry point that gives up the CPU to another task.

symbols.name: __schedule
symbols.purpose: Core scheduling logic that picks and switches tasks.

symbols.name: context_switch
symbols.purpose: Switches register state and address space between tasks.

areas.title: Memory management
areas.summary: Virtual memory areas, page faults, and physical page allocation.

symbols.name: do_mmap
symbols.purpose: Creates a new memory mapping for a process.

symbols.name: handle_mm_fault
symbols.purpose: Handles a page fault for a virtual address.

symbols.name: alloc_pages
symbols.purpose: Allocates contiguous physical pages.

areas.title: Virtual filesystem and filesystems
areas.summary: Path resolution and file opening, from the openat syscall to a filesystem's open callback.

symbols.name: do_sys_openat2
symbols.purpose: Common implementation behind openat and openat2.

symbols.name: do_filp_open
symbols.purpose: Resolves the final path component and opens the file.

symbols.name: vfs_open
symbols.purpose: Calls the filesystem's open handler with the resolved file.

areas.title: Block layer
areas.summary: Submission of block I/O and allocation of bios.

symbols.name: submit_bio
symbols.purpose: Submits a bio for block I/O.

symbols.name: blk_mq_submit_bio
symbols.purpose: Multi-queue submission path for a bio.

symbols.name: bio_alloc_bioset
symbols.purpose: Allocates a bio from a bioset.

areas.title: Networking
areas.summary: Packet receive and transmit paths in the network stack.

symbols.name: tcp_v4_rcv
symbols.purpose: Receive path for IPv4 TCP segments.

symbols.name: ip_rcv
symbols.purpose: Receive path for IPv4 packets.

symbols.name: __dev_queue_xmit
symbols.purpose: Transmits a packet on a network device.

areas.title: Device model and drivers
areas.summary: Device registration, driver binding, and bus management.

symbols.name: device_add
symbols.purpose: Registers a device with the device model.

symbols.name: bus_add_driver
symbols.purpose: Registers a driver with a bus.

symbols.name: __driver_probe_device
symbols.purpose: Attempts to bind a device to a driver.

areas.title: Architecture-specific code
areas.summary: Syscall entry and CPU setup for a target architecture (x86 shown; re-resolve for the target).

symbols.name: do_syscall_64
symbols.purpose: x86-64 syscall dispatch.

symbols.name: entry_SYSCALL_64
symbols.purpose: Assembly entry point for x86-64 syscalls.

symbols.name: start_kernel
symbols.purpose: Architecture-independent kernel startup entry.

areas.notes: x86 paths are an example; re-resolve against the target architecture before presenting.

areas.title: Boot and initialization
areas.summary: Kernel startup, init thread, and early initialization.

symbols.name: start_kernel
symbols.purpose: Main kernel startup function.

symbols.name: kernel_init
symbols.purpose: Init thread entry that runs /sbin/init.

symbols.name: rest_init
symbols.purpose: Spawns the init thread and becomes the idle task.

areas.title: Tracing and observability
areas.summary: Tracepoints, kprobes, and perf counters for observing kernel behavior.

symbols.name: register_kprobe
symbols.purpose: Registers a kprobe on a kernel address.

symbols.name: tracepoint_probe_register
symbols.purpose: Connects a probe to a tracepoint.

symbols.name: perf_event_create_kernel_counter
symbols.purpose: Creates a perf counter usable from kernel code.

areas.title: Security
areas.summary: Capability checks, permission decisions, and LSM hooks.

symbols.name: security_file_open
symbols.purpose: LSM hook invoked when a file is opened.

symbols.name: capable
symbols.purpose: Checks whether the current task has a capability.

symbols.name: ns_capable
symbols.purpose: Capability check relative to a user namespace.

areas.title: Inter-process communication
areas.summary: System V IPC: message queues, semaphores, and shared memory.

symbols.name: ksys_msgsnd
symbols.purpose: Kernel implementation of msgsnd(2).

symbols.name: ksys_msgrcv
symbols.purpose: Kernel implementation of msgrcv(2).

symbols.name: ksys_shmget
symbols.purpose: Kernel implementation of shmget(2).

symbols.name: ktime_get
symbols.purpose: Returns the current time as ktime_t.

symbols.name: hrtimer_start
symbols.purpose: Arms a high-resolution timer.

areas.title: Power management
areas.summary: System suspend/resume and runtime power management.

symbols.name: pm_suspend
symbols.purpose: Enters a system sleep state.

symbols.name: pm_runtime_get_sync
symbols.purpose: Increments runtime usage and resumes the device.

symbols.name: device_pm_add
symbols.purpose: Registers a device with the power management core.

symbols.name: kvm_init
symbols.purpose: Initializes the KVM subsystem.

symbols.name: kvm_vcpu_ioctl
symbols.purpose: Handles vCPU ioctls.
